children: Software firm Adobe Inc. (ADBE, Financials) is investing more than $4 billion in artificial intelligence projects in Saudi Arabia.
Adobe claimed that over 27 million eligible citizens and residents would enjoy 12 months of free access to its Firefly Standard subscription tier and Adobe Express Premium capabilities.

The program is part of a wider collaboration with Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology and government-backed AI firm HUMAIN. Adoption is the biggest problem for investors.
Adobe is sacrificing immediate subscription revenue to get its AI offerings into a wide market and create user habits before it charges customers later.

The deal also includes a new image-generation model developed in partnership with HUMAIN that is optimized for prompts in Arabic and will generate culturally relevant content. The move comes as Adobe faces growing competition from smaller, AI-native design platforms.

Free access for millions of users could help Adobe defend market share and drive engagement with Firefly and Express, but the real payoff depends on how many customers convert to paid subscriptions. The investors will be expecting large paid uptake once the 12 months free period in the Saudi launch is up.

title: Adobe Just Put $4 Billion Behind a Saudi AI Push
